page: Microsoft Azure M96-48bds_2_v3 is an x86_64 architecture server belonging to the MBDSMediumMemoryv3 family. It is powered by an Intel Xeon 8473C processor operating at 4.0 GHz, configured with 24 physical cores and 48 dedicated vCPUs via Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization. The hardware includes 1946.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high resource density of 40.54 GB per core. Local storage is provided by a 4608 GB SSD, and the instance is premium storage capable. No GPU accelerators are included.

In benchmark evaluations, the server demonstrates strong memory subsystem performance, with read-only small block memory bandwidth reaching 4147.11 GB/sec and large block write bandwidth at 156.64 GB/sec. Compute capabilities are highlighted by a Geekbench multi-core score of 19086.0 and a Passmark CPU score of 67646.12. The processor's Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) and AVX-512 support contribute to strong prompt processing speeds in LLM inference, achieving 2415.68 tokens/sec on small models and 28.01 tokens/sec on large models. However, text generation speeds for larger models are more moderate, averaging 3.54 tokens/sec.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the high memory-to-vCPU ratio and large local SSD capacity position this server as a resource-dense option for memory-bound workloads, reducing the need to scale out to larger vCPU counts solely for RAM. It is suited for large-scale database operations, in-memory caching systems like Redis (which achieved 66.02 million operations per second in testing), software compilation, and data-intensive enterprise applications.
